question: How many oxygen atoms are present in one molecule of ozone?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ozone** is a molecule made up o**f three oxygen atoms.**
 
• It smells very strongly and is a** light blue gas.**
 
• It is an oxygen allotrope that breaks down to** O₂** in the lower atmosphere and is **far less stable** than the diatomic allotrope O₂.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **2 oxygen atoms** is the number of oxygen atoms in a molecule of **oxygen gas (O₂).**
 
• **4 oxygen atoms** is the number of oxygen atoms in a molecule of **tetraoxygen (O₄),** which is an **unstable **allotrope of oxygen.
 
• **Oxygen's** atomic number is **eight **and its symbol is** O. **
 
 
• According to the periodic table, it belongs to the **chalcogen group.**
 
• It is a **nonmetal** that is **quite reactive. **
 
• It is an **oxidizing agent** that easily creates oxides with the majority of elements and other substances.
